evals.name: fresh-rn-repo-no-prior-agent-context
evals.prompt: I have a half-finished React Native app called WorkoutBuddy. It's a workout tracker — I've been vibe-coding it for a couple weeks and there's no AGENTS.md or guidelines folder yet. Wire up the standard agent context so Claude follows the course patterns when I work on it.
evals.expected_output: 11 files written to the repo root: AGENTS.md, best_practices.md, .agents/skills/README.md, guidelines/README.md + 8 guideline files (architecture, state, components, views, hooks, navigation, styling, skills). AGENTS.md heading reads 'AGENTS.md — WorkoutBuddy'. Stack is react-native.

evals.name: next-js-repo
evals.prompt: Wire up AGENTS.md on my Next.js project. It's a marketplace for vintage cameras called LensVault. Stack is Next.js 15 App Router with MUI.
evals.expected_output: Same 11 files. AGENTS.md heading reads 'AGENTS.md — LensVault'. Generated navigation.md is RN-specific so the next-steps message should remind the user to edit it to match Next.js App Router.

evals.name: refuses-to-overwrite-existing
evals.prompt: I have a repo at ./my-app that already has an AGENTS.md and a partial guidelines/ folder. I made some progress on the agent setup but want to redo it with the course's pattern. Wire it up.
evals.expected_output: The script preflights and finds the existing AGENTS.md (and possibly guidelines/README.md). It refuses to overwrite, prints the list of conflicting files, and tells the user to either rerun with --force yes OR edit the existing files manually. No files written.
